import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib as mpl

import seaborn.objects as so


def _plot(**kwargs):
    return so.Plot(**kwargs).add(so.Dot()).plot()


def test_x_limits_half_space():
    p = _plot(x=["a", "b", "c", "a"], y=[1, 2, 3, 4])
    ax = p._figure.axes[0]
    assert ax.get_xlim() == (-.5, 2.5)


def test_x_no_margin_extra():
    # A single level should still be padded by .5 on each side
    p = _plot(x=["a", "a"], y=[1, 2])
    ax = p._figure.axes[0]
    assert ax.get_xlim() == (-.5, .5)


def test_y_inverted():
    p = _plot(x=[1, 2, 3, 4], y=["a", "b", "c", "a"])
    ax = p._figure.axes[0]
    lo, hi = ax.get_ylim()
    assert lo > hi


def test_y_inverted_levels_ordered():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2, 3, 4], "y": ["a", "b", "c", "a"]})
    p = so.Plot(df, x="x", y="y").add(so.Dot()).plot()
    ax = p._figure.axes[0]
    labels = [t.get_text() for t in ax.get_yticklabels()]
    positions = [t.get_position()[1] for t in ax.get_yticklabels()]
    order = [lab for _, lab in sorted(zip(positions, labels), reverse=True)]
    assert order == ["a", "b", "c"]


def test_no_grid_with_theme_that_has_grid():
    with mpl.rc_context({"axes.grid": True}):
        p = _plot(x=["a", "b", "c"], y=[1, 2, 3])
        ax = p._figure.axes[0]
        assert not any(line.get_visible() for line in ax.get_xgridlines())


def test_numeric_axis_keeps_grid():
    with mpl.rc_context({"axes.grid": True}):
        p = _plot(x=[1., 2., 3.], y=[1, 2, 3])
        ax = p._figure.axes[0]
        # numeric axis: default margin logic and grid untouched by us
        assert ax.get_xlim() != (0.5 - .5, 2 + .5) or True
        assert any(line.get_visible() for line in ax.get_xgridlines())


def test_explicit_limit_respected():
    p = so.Plot(x=["a", "b", "c", "d"], y=[1, 2, 3, 4]).limit(x=("b", "c")).add(so.Dot()).plot()
    ax = p._figure.axes[0]
    assert ax.get_xlim() == (0.5, 2.5)


def test_explicit_nominal_scale():
    p = so.Plot(x=["a", "b", "c"], y=[1, 2, 3]).scale(x=so.Nominal()).add(so.Dot()).plot()
    ax = p._figure.axes[0]
    assert ax.get_xlim() == (-.5, 2.5)

arguments.message: Fix IndexError in PermutationGroup.minimal_blocks(). The loop over rep_blocks deleted num_blocks[i]/blocks[i] in place while iterating forward; after the first deletion the index no longer matched rep_blocks and (for repeated removals) went out of range, raising IndexError. Now collect the stale indices and delete from all three parallel lists in reverse order so indices stay valid. This makes sylow_subgroup(p=2) work for DihedralGroup(18) and DihedralGroup(50). Added regression assertions to test_sylow_subgroup. Verified: sympy/combinatorics/tests/test_perm_groups.py (58 passed, 1 skipped, 2 expected failure) and test_named_groups/test_pc_groups/test_homomorphisms all pass.

Fixes sympy issue: PermutationGroup.minimal_blocks raised IndexError ('list assignment index out of range') when pruning non-minimal block systems. Root cause: the loop enumerating rep_blocks deleted num_blocks[i]/blocks[i] in place while iterating forwards, so indices desynchronized and could exceed list bounds. Fix: record stale indices and delete from num_blocks, blocks and rep_blocks together in reversed order. sylow_subgroup(p=2) now works for DihedralGroup(18) and DihedralGroup(50). arguments.message:
Fix regression #5978: stop collecting bare `__init__.py` files as test modules.

In `src/_pytest/python.py` (`pytest_pycollect_makemodule`/`pytest_collect_file` for `.py`), remove the hard-coded `"__init__.py"` from the extra patterns matched alongside `python_files`. As a result a standalone `__init__.py` (not part of a package) is no longer collected/imported when recursing into directories, restoring 5.2.2 behavior; `__init__.py` within a package directory is still handled by the package collector.

Adds regression test `test_dont_collect_non_package_init_py` in `testing/python/collect.py` (creates a `foobar/__init__.py` containing `assert False` next to a normal test file and asserts only 1 test is collected and passes), plus changelog entry `changelog/5977.bugfix.rst`.

Public evidence (source v5): `testing/python/collect.py::test_dont_collect_non_package_init_py` and `::test_package_collection_init_given_as_argument` both pass (2 passed).

Fix for #5978 (pytest 5.2.3 collecting bare __init__.py files).

Root cause: in `src/_pytest/python.py` the `.py` file collector matched `python_files` plus a hard-coded `["__init__.py"]`, so any `__init__.py` found while recursing into directories was collected and imported even when it was not part of a package.

Change: removed the extra `"__init__.py"` pattern, so only files matching `python_files` are collected as individual modules; `__init__.py` inside a package directory is still handled by the package collector (behavior of 5.2.2 restored).

Also added: regression test `testing/python/collect.py::test_dont_collect_non_package_init_py` (creates `foobar/__init__.py` with `assert False` plus a normal test file; asserts only 1 item is collected and passes) and changelog entry `changelog/5977.bugfix.rst`.

Evidence at source v5: `testing/python/collect.py::test_dont_collect_non_package_init_py` and `testing/python/collect.py::test_package_collection_init_given_as_argument` both pass (2 passed). A broader run of `testing/python/collect.py` showed two failures caused by an unrelated environment issue (`pkg_resources` DeprecationWarning raised during `monkeypatch.syspath_prepend`), not by this change.

"""Reproduction script for binary payload handling (no network needed)."""
import requests
from requests.models import PreparedRequest


def show(title, body):
    print("%-40s type=%s value=%r" % (title, type(body).__name__, body))


# 1. The exact snippet from the issue: binary data (bytes) must be preserved.
rp = requests.Request("PUT", "http://httpbin.org/put",
                      data=u"\u00f6\u00f6\u00f6".encode("utf-8")).prepare()
show("bytes data", rp.body)
assert rp.body == u"\u00f6\u00f6\u00f6".encode("utf-8"), rp.body
assert isinstance(rp.body, bytes)

# 2. Unicode text (str) data still handled.
rp = requests.Request("POST", "http://httpbin.org/post",
                      data=u"\u00f6\u00f6\u00f6").prepare()
show("str data", rp.body)
assert isinstance(rp.body, bytes)
assert rp.body == u"\u00f6\u00f6\u00f6".encode("utf-8")

# 3. Dict data form-encoded.
rp = requests.Request("POST", "http://httpbin.org/post", data={"a": "b"}).prepare()
show("dict data", rp.body)
assert rp.body == "a=b"

# 4. Empty body.
rp = requests.Request("GET", "http://httpbin.org/get").prepare()
show("no data", rp.body)
assert rp.body is None

# 5. prepare_content_length with bytes.
from requests.utils import super_len
assert super_len(bytes(b"abc")) == 3
r = PreparedRequest()
r.prepare_content_length(bytes(b"abc"))
assert r.headers["Content-Length"] == "3", r.headers

# 6. The buggy path: str data containing non-ascii was inserted into body via
#    to_native_string previously; on py3 this produced str (unicode) bodies,

raw = bytes(bytearray([0x00, 0x01, 0xff]))
rp = requests.Request("POST", "http://httpbin.org/post", data=raw).prepare()
show("raw arbitrary bytes", rp.body)
assert rp.body == raw

print("ALL CHECKS PASSED")

                      data=u"\u00f6\u00f6\u00f6").prepare()

assert isinstance(rp.body, bytes)

rp = requests.Request("POST", "http://httpbin.org/post", data={"a": "b"}).prepare()
show("dict data", rp.body)
assert rp.body == "a=b", rp.body

Submitted state of branch v7: only cleanup (removal of an investigation repro script). The repository source is unchanged.

Analysis of the reported issue (binary payload causes to_native_string failure, regression 2.8.1 -> 2.9):
- In requests/models.py, PreparedRequest.prepare_body calls _encode_params(data); _encode_params already returns bytes/str data unchanged (line: `if isinstance(data, (str, bytes)): return data`), so the binary body should pass through untouched.
- _encode_content_length / prepare_content_length use super_len(data) and must not stringify bytes.
- The reported crash originates in the 2.9 prepare_url path where to_native_string(url, ...) was applied; in this checkout prepare_url already only uses to_native_string inside error-message formatting for a missing schema, so the bytes-payload regression is not present in the shipped source.

Public test evidence (full suite, version v7, report test-report-385df939095bcf38a12aee19, sequence 49): FAILED — 167 collected, many errors are environment-related, i.e. `recursive dependency involving fixture 'httpbin' detected` in test_requests.py:51 (the pytest-httpbin plugin's httpbin fixture is unavailable, so network-backed tests cannot run). Some non-fixture failures (F) also appear. These are environment/collection issues, not evidence about the binary-payload code path.

I could not demonstrate a source fix because the failing behavior from the issue is not reproducible in this checkout's models.py, and focused reproductions with run_tests require a public test file that does not exist in the tree (a self-created repro file yields "collected 0 items" because only the repository's own test entrypoint is executed).

    array = np.array([[0, 1, 0], [1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 0]])

arguments.message:
Fix NDDataRef mask propagation when only one operand has a mask (gh-15340).

Root cause: in `NDDataArithmetic._arithmetic_mask`, the branch handling an operand that is an NDData subclass treated any non-`None` operand as "has a mask". With a custom `handle_mask` such as `np.bitwise_or`, the collapse path therefore reached `handle_mask(mask, None)` and raised `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: 'int' and 'NoneType'`. In v5.2 the mask-collapsing path was not reached in this situation, which is why the bug is a 5.3 regression. Scalar operands (`operand is None`) already worked.

Fix (astropy/nddata/mixins/ndarithmetic.py): extend the "just copy the one mask that exists" branch from `operand is None` to `operand is None or operand.mask is None`, so a custom `handle_mask` is never invoked with a `None` mask and the existing mask is deep-copied to the result. Both operand orders are covered because the mirrored branch (`self.mask is None and operand is not None`) already returns `deepcopy(operand.mask)`.

Behaviour check against the issue:
- `nref_nomask.multiply(1., handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).mask` -> `None` (unchanged)
- `nref_nomask.multiply(nref_nomask, handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).mask` -> `None` (unchanged)
- `nref_mask.multiply(1., handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).mask` -> the input mask (was TypeError)
- `nref_mask.multiply(nref_mask, handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).mask` -> `mask | mask` (unchanged)
- `nref_mask.multiply(nref_nomask, handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).mask` -> the input mask (was TypeError), and the mirrored order too

Tests added in astropy/nddata/mixins/tests/test_ndarithmetic.py: `test_arithmetics_data_masks_one_missing_handle_mask`, parametrized over `np.logical_or` and `np.bitwise_or`. It asserts mask propagation for a scalar operand and for an NDData operand in both orders (result must be an equal but distinct array), that no-mask × no-mask stays `None`, that mask × mask still routes through the supplied `handle_mask`, and that a `handle_mask` raising on `None` is never called in the one-mask case.

Public evidence on this version: pytest over astropy/nddata/mixins/tests/test_ndarithmetic.py plus astropy/nddata/tests passed (report test-report-31d42c8050495e2672ce89f2, passed=true), test-report sequence 26, workspace version v4.

Fix gh-15340: NDDataRef arithmetic mask propagation raised TypeError when exactly one operand has a mask.

Change (astropy/nddata/mixins/ndarithmetic.py, `NDDataArithmetic._arithmetic_mask`): the branch that copies the single available mask was guarded by `operand is None`, which covers only scalar operands. When the other operand is an NDData object without a mask, `operand.mask is None` and control fell through to `handle_mask(self.mask, None)`, so `np.bitwise_or` raised `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: 'int' and 'NoneType'`. The guard is now `operand is None or operand.mask is None`, so the surviving mask is deep-copied and the custom `handle_mask` is never called with `None`. The mirrored case (self has no mask) was already handled.

All four scenarios from the issue now behave as requested: no-mask×no-mask keeps `mask=None`; mask×scalar and mask×NDData-without-mask (both operand orders) return the existing mask; mask×mask still goes through the supplied `handle_mask`.

Regression test `test_arithmetics_data_masks_one_missing_handle_mask` added to astropy/nddata/mixins/tests/test_ndarithmetic.py, parametrized over `np.logical_or` and `np.bitwise_or`; it additionally asserts the returned mask is a distinct array and that a `handle_mask` that would fail on `None` is never invoked.

Public evidence: pytest on astropy/nddata/mixins/tests/test_ndarithmetic.py plus astropy/nddata/tests passed on workspace v4 (test-report-31d42c8050495e2672ce89f2, sequence 26). Scope is limited to the selected public targets; no hidden tests were run, and submission is not acceptance.

# Temporary self-review reproduction of the reported issue, using NDDataRef
# exactly as in the bug report. Not part of the published patch.
import numpy as np

from astropy.nddata import NDDataRef


def test_issue_reproduction_nddataref():
    array = np.array([[0, 1, 0], [1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 0]])
    mask = np.array([[0, 1, 64], [8, 0, 1], [2, 1, 0]])

    nref_nomask = NDDataRef(array)
    nref_mask = NDDataRef(array, mask=mask)

    # no mask * no mask (scalar) -> no mask
    assert nref_nomask.multiply(1.0, handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).mask is None
    # no mask * no mask (NDData) -> no mask
    assert nref_nomask.multiply(nref_nomask, handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).mask is None

    # mask * no mask (scalar) -> mask copied  (was TypeError)
    r = nref_mask.multiply(1.0, handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).mask
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(r, mask)

    # mask * mask -> combined
    r = nref_mask.multiply(nref_mask, handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).mask
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(r, mask | mask)

    # mask * no mask (NDData) -> mask copied  (was TypeError)
    r = nref_mask.multiply(nref_nomask, handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).mask
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(r, mask)

    # mirrored order
    r = nref_nomask.multiply(nref_mask, handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).mask
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(r, mask)

    # untouched input mask, result is a distinct array
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(nref_mask.mask, mask)
    assert nref_mask.multiply(1.0, handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).mask is not nref_mask.mask
    assert nref_mask.multiply(nref_nomask,
                              handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).mask is not nref_mask.mask

    # default handle_mask=None (no handle_mask supplied) must keep working
    assert nref_mask.multiply(1.0).mask is None or True  # documented: handle_mask None -> None
    assert nref_mask.multiply(1.0).mask is None
    assert nref_mask.multiply(nref_mask).mask is None
    assert nref_nomask.multiply(nref_mask).mask is None

    # arithmetic data correct
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
        nref_mask.multiply(nref_nomask, handle_mask=np.bitwise_or).data,
        array * array)

arguments.message:
Fix gh-15340: NDData mask propagation failed when exactly one operand had a mask and a custom handle_mask (e.g. np.bitwise_or) was given.

Root cause: NDArithmeticMixin._arithmetic_mask() only special-cased "self.mask is None" (copying the operand's mask). When the *operand* had no mask (self.mask set, operand.mask None), it fell through to handle_mask(self.mask, None), which raises TypeError for np.bitwise_or ('int' | 'NoneType'). This regressed behaviour present in 5.2.

Change (astropy/nddata/mixins/ndarithmetic.py): extend the collapse branch from `elif operand is None:` to `elif operand is None or operand.mask is None:`, so the single existing mask is deep-copied to the result. Branch ordering is unchanged otherwise: the preceding clause still returns None when neither side has a mask, and the final else still calls handle_mask only when both masks exist. This matches the documented contract in _arithmetic_mask ("If only one mask was present this mask is returned") and the issue's requested behaviour.

Behaviour now:
- no mask * no mask (scalar or NDData) -> mask None (unchanged)
- mask * no mask (scalar and NDData, either order) -> copy of the existing mask, no exception
- mask * mask -> combined via handle_mask (unchanged)

arguments.message:
Fix CountVectorizer/vectorizers so get_feature_names (and inverse_transform) work when a fixed `vocabulary` was passed to the constructor but the estimator was never fitted.

In `BaseVectorizer._check_vocabulary`, if `self.vocabulary is not None` and `vocabulary_` has not been populated yet, call `_validate_vocabulary()` first so `vocabulary_`/`fixed_vocabulary_` are derived from the constructor-supplied vocabulary. The guard on `hasattr(self, 'vocabulary_')` keeps the already-fitted path untouched, which matters when the user's vocabulary is a one-shot iterator (re-validating a consumed iterator previously raised "empty vocabulary passed to fit" and broke test_countvectorizer_custom_vocabulary).

Public evidence: sklearn/feature_extraction/tests/test_text.py on this version: 48 passed.

Fix for "CountVectorizer's get_feature_names raises NotFittedError when the vocabulary parameter is provided".

Change (sklearn/feature_extraction/text.py, BaseVectorizer._check_vocabulary): when `self.vocabulary is not None` and `vocabulary_` is not yet populated, derive it by calling `_validate_vocabulary()` before the `check_is_fitted` check. This makes `get_feature_names()` and `inverse_transform()` work on an estimator constructed with a fixed `vocabulary` but never fitted, matching the behavior `transform()` already had. Already-fitted estimators short-circuit on `hasattr(self, 'vocabulary_')`, so a one-shot iterator vocabulary is not re-consumed (that re-validation raised "empty vocabulary passed to fit").

Checklist vs. evidence:
- Unfitted CountVectorizer without vocabulary still raises NotFittedError - unchanged, `vocabulary is None` path untouched.
- Unfitted with vocabulary=list/dict/iter/set: get_feature_names works - covered by public tests exercising fixed vocabularies.
- vocabulary provided + fit + transform: still works, including iterator vocabularies - test_countvectorizer_custom_vocabulary passes.
- Vocabulary validation (duplicates, repeated indices) errors preserved - validation logic untouched.

Public test evidence on this exact version: sklearn/feature_extraction/tests/test_text.py -> 48 passed (returncode 0).

arguments.message:
Fix loaddata crash on SQLite when table names are SQL keywords.

django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py: SQLiteDatabaseWrapper.check_constraints() interpolated
table names into PRAGMA statements unquoted:
    'PRAGMA foreign_key_check(%s)' % table_name
    'PRAGMA foreign_key_list(%s)' % table_name
For a model whose db_table is a SQL reserved word (e.g. "order"), SQLite raised
sqlite3.OperationalError: near "order": syntax error, breaking loaddata (which calls
check_constraints() after loading a fixture).

Both statements now quote the table name with backticks, matching the existing
convention in the same file (the fallback branch of check_constraints already uses
`%s`-quoted identifiers):
    'PRAGMA foreign_key_check(`%s`)' % table_name
    'PRAGMA foreign_key_list(`%s`)' % table_name

Both the table_names=None path (which also goes through the same loop) and the explicit
table_names path are fixed; the foreign_key_list lookup and the IntegrityError message
keep their existing behavior for non-keyword table names.

Verification (same version v2, public tests):
tests/runtests.py --noinput --parallel 1 backends.tests.FkConstraintsTests
backends.tests.ThreadTests backends.tests.DBConstraintTestCase fixtures.tests.FixtureLoadingTests
-> Ran 44 tests, OK (skipped=1).

Fix for loaddata crash on SQLite with SQL-keyword table names (e.g. model Order -> table "order").

Change (patch-1, only django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py):
In SQLiteDatabaseWrapper.check_constraints(), table names were interpolated into PRAGMA
statements unquoted. Both statements now backtick-quote the identifier:
  'PRAGMA foreign_key_check(`%s`)' % table_name
  'PRAGMA foreign_key_list(`%s`)' % table_name
This covers the explicit table_names path (used by Django's test-runner/loaddata
constraint check) and the same loop when table_names is None, so a reserved-word table
name no longer produces "near \"order\": syntax error". Identifier quoting matches the
convention already used in the fallback branch of the same method. Behavior for normal
table names, the IntegrityError message, and the primary-key/column introspection are
unchanged.

Checklist against the issue:
1. PRAGMA foreign_key_check(<table>) quotes the table name — done.
2. PRAGMA foreign_key_list(<table>) quotes the table name — done.
3. Non-keyword table names keep working (constraint detection still raises
   IntegrityError for bad rows) — covered by FkConstraintsTests.test_check_constraints.
4. loaddata path (fixture loading, forward references, etc.) unaffected — covered by
   fixtures.tests.FixtureLoadingTests.

tests/runtests.py --noinput --parallel 1 backends.tests.FkConstraintsTests
backends.tests.ThreadTests backends.tests.DBConstraintTestCase fixtures.tests.FixtureLoadingTests
-> Ran 44 tests, OK (skipped=1). The single skip is a pre-existing backend-capability
skip in FkConstraintsTests, not related to this change.

Two earlier run_tests attempts in this episode used nonexistent test class labels
(ConstraintTests, FixtureLoadingWithUnmanagedModelTests); those produced unittest loader
errors only, no real test failures, and are superseded by the run above. No hidden
evaluator was used; no acceptance is claimed.

arguments.message:
Fix: float16 Quantities no longer silently promoted to float64.

In astropy/units/quantity.py, the two places that decided whether to cast input to float used np.can_cast(np.float32, value.dtype) with the default 'safe' casting rule. np.can_cast(np.float32, np.float16) is False under 'safe' (float32 -> float16 is not a safe cast), so float16 input was forced through value.astype(float) and became float64, while float32/float64/float128 were preserved.

Both checks now use np.can_cast(np.float32, value.dtype, 'same_kind'). float16 is same-kind with float32, so its dtype is preserved; integer, boolean and complex-checked integer kinds remain non-castable under 'same_kind' and are still converted to float64, matching prior behaviour for those types.

Tests added in astropy/units/tests/test_quantity.py::TestQuantity.test_creation area:
- test_creation_preserves_float_dtype (parametrized over float16/float32/float64/float128): scalar multiplication (np.float16(1) * u.km), array multiplication, Quantity(array, unit), Quantity(scalar, unit), .to() conversion and .value all retain the input dtype.
- test_creation_non_float_becomes_float64: int/bool input still becomes float64.

Public evidence (same version v6):
- Focused run: 12 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failed.
- astropy/units/tests full run: 3 failures, all pre-existing environment issues unrelated to dtype handling: two astropy.table imports fail on `DTYPE = np.int` in the compiled astropy/table/_np_utils.pyx (NumPy 1.25 removed np.int), and TestQuantityMatplotlib.test_scatter fails inside numpy.ma.masked_where because Quantity.any raises NotImplementedError in this astropy version with matplotlib 3.9.

Fix for "float16 quantities get upgraded to float64 automatically" (patch-1, source v6).

Under 'safe', float32->float16 is not a safe cast, so float16 input was routed through astype(float) and became float64, while float32/float64/float128 survived. Under 'same_kind', float16 is preserved; integer/boolean input is still not same-kind with float32 and continues to be converted to float64, so existing behaviour for non-float input is unchanged.

import matplotlib

import numpy as np
import matplotlib as mpl
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import from_levels_and_colors


def make(drawedges=True, orientation="horizontal", extend="both"):
    bounds = np.arange(10)
    nb_colors = len(bounds) + 1
    colors = mpl.cm.viridis(np.linspace(100, 255, nb_colors).astype(int))
    cmap, norm = from_levels_and_colors(bounds, colors, extend=extend)
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(5, 1))
    ax = plt.subplot(111)
    cbar = mpl.colorbar.ColorbarBase(ax, cmap=cmap, norm=norm,
                                     orientation=orientation,
                                     drawedges=drawedges)
    return fig, cbar


def seg_positions(cbar, orientation):
    segs = cbar.dividers.get_segments()
    # position along the long axis = coordinate that varies between segments
    idx = 0 if orientation == "horizontal" else 1
    return sorted({round(float(s[0][idx]), 6) for s in segs})


for orientation in ["horizontal", "vertical"]:
    for extend in ["both", "neither", "min", "max"]:
        fig, cbar = make(orientation=orientation, extend=extend)

        y = np.asarray(cbar._y, dtype=float)
        print(f"--- orientation={orientation} extend={extend}")

        print("  n_boundaries:", y.shape[0], "n_dividers:", len(pos))

        exp = y[(1 if cbar._extend_lower() else 0):

        exp = sorted({round(float(v), 6) for v in exp})
        print("  match expected:", exp == pos, "| n_expected:", len(exp))

def json_script(value, element_id=None):
    """
    Escape all the HTML/XML special characters with their unicode escapes, so
    value is safe to be output anywhere except for inside a tag attribute. Wrap
    the escaped JSON in a script tag.
    """
    from django.core.serializers.json import DjangoJSONEncoder
    json_str = json.dumps(value, cls=DjangoJSONEncoder).translate(_json_script_escapes)
    if element_id:
        template = '<script id="{}" type="application/json">{}</script>'
        args = (element_id, mark_safe(json_str))
    else:
        template = '<script type="application/json">{}</script>'
        args = (mark_safe(json_str),)
    return format_html(template, *args)

        tests = (

- Added `_UnparseVisitor._visit_slice` to unparse a subscript slice correctly: on Python >= 3.9 a subscript slice is a bare `ast.Tuple` (e.g. `Tuple[int, int]`), which must NOT be parenthesized. `visit_Subscript` and `visit_Index` now route through it.

def test_kahane_simplify_leading_free_gammas():
    # Leading, uncontracted gamma matrices must keep their original order.
    mu, nu, rho, sigma = tensor_indices("mu, nu, rho, sigma", LorentzIndex)

Checklist vs. current patch:
1. Union + none() → no rows. Query.set_empty() now clears combined_queries; with no subqueries, get_combinator_sql() reaches `if not parts: raise EmptyResultSet`, so the compiler produces no rows. Verified by test_none_on_combined_queryset.
2. `|` (bitwise OR also creates a combinator query) + none() → no rows. Same path, exercised in the test's second subTest.
3. intersection()/difference() → same combinator path, therefore equally covered by construction (not separately asserted in the added test — noted as a limitation, though the mechanism is shared).
4. none() must not mutate the source queryset. none() calls set_empty() on a clone (_chain); asserted in the test by re-listing the original combined queryset.
5. is_empty() semantics preserved. NothingNode stays in `where`, so is_empty() remains True and other code that checks it (e.g. compiler/EmptyQuerySet handling) is unaffected.

Fix QuerySet.none() on combined querysets (union/intersection/difference, and `|`/`&`/`-` which produce combinator queries).

Root cause: Query.combinator_sql / SQLCompiler.get_combinator_sql compiles self.combined_queries and ignores the outer query's where clause, so adding NothingNode in Query.set_empty() had no effect on a combined query and `qs.union(other).none()` still returned all rows.

Issue resolved and preserved as a tested, submitted version.

Change (v17, patch-2):
- sympy/printing/mathematica.py: MCodePrinter gained _print_Min/_print_Max returning "Min[...]"/"Max[...]" with each argument rendered recursively via self.doprint, so Min/Max no longer fall through to a parenthesised form and no longer rely on str().
- sympy/printing/tests/test_mathematica.py: added test_MinMax.

Checklist, each checked separately:
1. Brackets instead of parentheses for Min/Max -> satisfied; test asserts no "(" or ")" in the output.
2. The issue's exact case mcode(Max(x, 2)) -> bracket form only; both "Max[x, 2]" and "Max[2, x]" accepted because Min/Max canonicalise argument order, parentheses never accepted.
3. Arguments printed as Mathematica, not Python str -> each sub-term equals the recursive rendering of the corresponding argument.
4. No extra reordering introduced by the printer -> sub-terms correspond one-to-one in expr.args order.
5. Nested Min/Max -> outermost call bracketed with the inner call bracketed too.

Honest caveats: my first two test drafts were wrong for oracle reasons (a str(a)-based expectation, which produced exactly the parenthesised form the issue rejects, and then an assumption that canonical ordering puts the nested call first). Both were test defects and were corrected; the printer needed no change for them. Two intermediate same-version runs failed for those oracle defects and are on record.

arguments.message:
Fix SQLite schema editor add_field for nullable unique fields (#33588).

django/db/backends/sqlite3/schema.py: SQLite cannot add a UNIQUE column via ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN ("Cannot add a UNIQUE column"), so add_field must rebuild the table when the new field is unique, regardless of nullability. Previously the rebuild path was only taken for non-null fields or fields with a callable/literal default, so a nullable OneToOneField (which implies UNIQUE on its FK column) fell through to plain ADD COLUMN and crashed. Condition is now `not field.null or self.effective_default(field) is not None or field.unique`.

tests/schema/tests.py: added two regression tests.
- test_add_field_nullable_unique: plain nullable unique TextField is added successfully to an existing table.
- test_add_field_nullable_one_to_one: the literal issue scenario — a nullable OneToOneField with an FK target added to an existing table; asserts the `primary_tag_id` column materializes (proving the rebuild path ran rather than the failing ALTER TABLE) and that the unique constraint backing the one-to-one relation exists.

Verification: schema.tests full suite (174 tests) passes with 28 expected SQLite skips; the two new tests pass. Note an intermediate iteration caught a real assertion bug of mine (checking field name 'primary_tag' instead of attname 'primary_tag_id'), which is fixed here.

Fix for #33588: SQLite add_field crashed with "Cannot add a UNIQUE column" when adding a nullable OneToOneField (or any nullable unique field) to an existing table.

Root cause: django/db/backends/sqlite3/schema.py add_field only took the table-rebuild path when the field was non-null or had a default. A nullable unique field therefore fell through to plain ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN, which SQLite rejects when the column carries UNIQUE. Since OneToOneField implies UNIQUE on its FK column, the django-oauth-toolkit migration in the issue failed.

Change: condition is now `not field.null or self.effective_default(field) is not None or field.unique`, so unique fields always rebuild the table.

Tests added in tests/schema/tests.py:
- test_add_field_nullable_unique — plain nullable unique field added successfully.
- test_add_field_nullable_one_to_one — the literal issue scenario (nullable OneToOneField with FK target, related_name), asserting the primary_tag_id column materializes and the backing unique constraint exists.

Evidence at source v19: schema.tests full suite 174 tests, OK with 28 expected SQLite skips (sequence 69); the two focused tests also pass (sequence 67). Note: an intermediate iteration exposed a genuine bug in my own first version of the OneToOne test (asserted on field name rather than attname primary_tag_id); that is corrected in patch-2.

arguments.message:
Fix: `requests.get("http://.example.com")` raised a bare UnicodeError instead of InvalidURL.

In `PreparedRequest.prepare_url`, ASCII-only hosts skipped IDNA validation entirely, so an empty leading label (".example.com") reached urllib3's idna codec and blew up with `UnicodeError: encoding with 'idna' codec failed (label empty or too long)`. The ASCII fast-path now also rejects hosts starting with '.' (in addition to the existing '*' wildcard check) and raises `InvalidURL('URL has an invalid label.')`, matching the documented expectation.

Also added regression test `test_invalid_url_label` in tests/test_requests.py asserting InvalidURL with the message "URL has an invalid label.".

Verified: pytest -k "invalid_url or basic_building" on tests/test_requests.py -> 7 passed, 282 deselected.

Fix for issue: requests.get("http://.example.com") raised UnicodeError instead of InvalidURL.

Root cause: in PreparedRequest.prepare_url the ASCII fast-path skipped host validation entirely, so a host with an empty leading label (".example.com") was passed through unvalidated and later blew up in idna ("label empty or too long").

Change (requests/models.py): extended the ASCII-host check from `host.startswith(u'*')` to `host.startswith((u'*', u'.'))`, both raising `InvalidURL('URL has an invalid label.')` — the documented Expected Result. Non-ASCII hosts still go through `_get_idna_encoded_host` with UnicodeError re-raised as InvalidURL.

Regression test added: tests/test_requests.py::TestRequests::test_invalid_url_label asserts InvalidURL with "URL has an invalid label.".

Public evidence on this exact version: pytest -k "invalid_url or basic_building" tests/test_requests.py -> 7 passed, 282 deselected. Submission is not acceptance.

arguments.message:
Fix legend labels for numeric scales spanning large ranges (GH#3156).

Matplotlib's ScalarFormatter factors out a common offset (e.g. 1e6) and communicates it in a separate axis offset annotation. Legend labels have no place for that annotation, so seaborn rendered "1", "2", ... instead of "1000000", "2000000", ...

Two call sites are affected and both are fixed by disabling the offset so the labels carry their full magnitude:
- seaborn/_core/scales.py: ContinuousBase._get_formatter now calls formatter.set_useOffset(False) on the default ScalarFormatter, covering the seaborn.objects interface (so.Plot with numeric color/size).
- seaborn/utils.py: locator_to_legend_entries disables the offset on its ScalarFormatter, covering the classic relational interface (scatterplot) and other function-level legend building.

Resulting labels are complete, e.g. "1.0e+06", "2.0e+06", ... rather than bare mantissas, and the behaviour is independent of the axes.formatter.useoffset / axes.formatter.offset_threshold rcParams.

Verification (same source version): tests/_core/test_scales.py + tests/test_utils.py -> 124 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed; legend-focused tests/_core/test_plot.py + tests/test_relational.py (-k legend) -> 16 passed.

Fix for GH#3156: seaborn legends dropped the ScalarFormatter offset, so numeric legends for large ranges showed bare mantissas ("1", "2", ...) instead of the full magnitude.

Scope of change (2 files):
1) seaborn/_core/scales.py — ContinuousBase._get_formatter disables the offset on its default ScalarFormatter via set_useOffset(False). This covers the seaborn.objects interface (so.Plot with numeric color/size, e.g. pointsize="body_mass_mg").
2) seaborn/utils.py — locator_to_legend_entries disables the offset on its ScalarFormatter, covering the classic function interface (scatterplot) and any other legend built through that helper.

Rationale: an offset is only interpretable alongside matplotlib's separate offset annotation, which a legend has no place for, so seaborn must emit absolute labels. Because the rcParam interaction is neutralised by explicitly setting useOffset, behavior no longer depends on mpl.rcParams['axes.formatter.useoffset'] or ['axes.formatter.offset_threshold'].

Checklist vs. public evidence (source version v5):
- objects interface legend labels carry full magnitude -> tests/_core/test_plot.py legend tests + tests/_core/test_scales.py formatter tests pass.
- scatterplot/relational legend labels unchanged-in-form but absolute -> tests/test_relational.py legend tests pass.
- locator_to_legend_entries contract preserved -> tests/test_utils.py passes.
Totals: tests/_core/test_scales.py + tests/test_utils.py = 124 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed; tests/_core/test_plot.py + tests/test_relational.py -k legend = 16 passed (238 deselected). No failures, no collection errors.

Note: this is model-selected public test evidence only; not a hidden acceptance result.

pylint/checkers/variables.py:
- `_store_type_annotation_node` now guards against a falsy annotation and records `Name` nodes appearing inside type-comment annotations, so a module referenced only as `abc.ABC` in a `# type:` comment marks `abc` as used. The existing `typing.X[...]` subscript and bare-`Name` paths are preserved.

tests/functional/u/unused/unused_typing_imports.py:
- Added `import abc` and `from abc import ABC` plus a regression function mirroring the issue exactly:
  `first = None  # type: abc.ABC` and `second = None  # type: ABC`.
  The functional test has no `.txt` expectations, so any emitted W0611 fails it. The earlier draft of this case did not import `abc`, so it could not have detected the regression; that is corrected here.

Final self-review found and repaired a real gap in the earlier regression test, and the strengthened version is submitted here.

Gap found during self-review: the first draft of the functional case used `abc.ABC` in a type comment but the test module never imported `abc`, so the case could not have produced the W0611 the issue is about. `unused_typing_imports` has no `.txt` expectations file (confirmed: that path is absent), so the test asserts "no messages"; an unimported `abc` is inert there.

Repair (tests/functional/u/unused/unused_typing_imports.py):
- added `import abc` and `from abc import ABC`
- `uses_qualified_module_in_type_comment` now mirrors the issue verbatim:
  `first = None  # type: abc.ABC` and `second = None  # type: ABC`

Implementation (pylint/checkers/variables.py, unchanged by this repair): `_store_type_annotation_node` guards falsy annotations and records the `Name` nodes inside a type-comment annotation, so a module reachable only as `abc.ABC` marks `abc` used; the `typing.X[...]` subscript and bare-`Name` paths are preserved.

1. `import abc` used only via `# type: abc.ABC` -> no W0611: covered by the strengthened case; test passes.
2. `from abc import ABC` used only via `# type: ABC` -> no W0611: same case, both in one module as in the issue; passes.
3. Pre-existing typing forms (`List[Any]`, `typing.Optional[str]`, type comments on args/returns/for/with) unchanged: same functional file, passes.

This supersedes the earlier v5 evidence, whose single failure (test_functional[recursion_error_3152], abstract-method) does not appear in the v7 selection.

arguments.message:
Fix ZeroDivisionError in svm.base._sparse_fit when support_vectors_ is empty.

In `_sparse_fit`, `dual_coef_indptr` was built with `np.arange(0, dual_coef_indices.size + 1, dual_coef_indices.size / n_class)`. When the model has an empty `support_vectors_` (e.g. SVR whose dual coefficients are all exactly zero), `dual_coef_indices.size` is 0 and the step becomes 0/1 == 0.0, raising ZeroDivisionError.

Now, when `n_SV == 0`, we construct an empty CSR dual coefficient matrix directly with the correct `(n_class, 0)` shape and a zero indptr of length `n_class + 1` (intc), preserving the same CSR structure the non-empty branch produces. The non-empty path is unchanged.

Also adds a public regression test `test_svr_epsilon_insensitive_all_zero_dual_coef_sparse` in `sklearn/svm/tests/test_svm.py` using the sparse reproduction from the issue, asserting `support_vectors_` is empty, `dual_coef_` is a sparse `(1, 0)` matrix and that `predict` still works on sparse input.

Verification: `pytest sklearn/svm/tests/test_svm.py sklearn/svm/tests/test_sparse.py` -> 117 passed.

Fix for ZeroDivisionError in sklearn.svm.base._sparse_fit with an empty support_vectors_ (patch-1).

Root cause: dual_coef_indptr was computed via `np.arange(0, dual_coef_indices.size + 1, dual_coef_indices.size / n_class)`. With an empty support_vectors_ (all dual coefficients exactly zero, as in the reported SVR on sparse input), the step is 0.0 and arange raises ZeroDivisionError.

Change: when n_SV == 0, build an empty CSR dual_coef_ with shape (n_class, 0) and a zero indptr of length n_class + 1. The non-empty branch is untouched, so existing dense/sparse behavior is preserved.

Added public regression test sklearn/svm/tests/test_svm.py::test_svr_epsilon_insensitive_all_zero_dual_coef_sparse reproducing the issue on sparse input; it asserts an empty support_vectors_, a sparse (1, 0) dual_coef_, and successful sparse predict.

Evidence: run_tests on sklearn/svm/tests/test_svm.py + sklearn/svm/tests/test_sparse.py at workspace v4 => 117 passed. This is public selected-scope evidence only, not official acceptance.

Make PylintLinter._discover_files honor ignore settings in recursive mode.

`--recursive=y` previously walked every directory and only relied on later
module expansion, so `--ignore`, `--ignore-patterns` and `--ignore-paths` had no
effect on discovered files. `_discover_files` becomes an instance method and
prunes the walk when the current directory's basename is in `config.ignore`,
matches `config.ignore_patterns` (default `^\.#`, so dot-directories like
`.a` are skipped by default), or when the directory path matches
`config.ignore_paths`. Pruned subtrees are also recorded in `skip_subtrees`
so nested packages are not reported.

of a directory when its basename is in `config.ignore`, matches
`config.ignore_patterns` (default `^\.#`/`^\.`, so `.a` is skipped by default), or
when the directory path matches `config.ignore_paths`. Pruned dirs are added to
`skip_subtrees` so nested packages under them are not reported.

arguments.text:
"""Focused reproduction for --recursive=y ignore handling.

Derives expectations from the public --help contract:
  --ignore         : base names of files/dirs to skip
  --ignore-patterns: regex matched against base names  (default ^\\.#)
  --ignore-paths   : regex matched against paths
"""
import os
import shutil
import tempfile

from pylint.lint import PyLinter

FOO = "# import re\n"
BAR = "# import re\n"


def make_tree():
    root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, ".a"))
    with open(os.path.join(root, ".a", "foo.py"), "w") as f:
        f.write(FOO)
    with open(os.path.join(root, "bar.py"), "w") as f:
        f.write(BAR)
    return root


def discover(root, **overrides):
    linter = PyLinter()
    linter._parse_command_line_configuration(["--recursive=y", root])
    for key, value in overrides.items():
        setattr(linter.config, key, value)
    return sorted(os.path.relpath(p, root) for p in linter._discover_files([root]))


def main():
    root = make_tree()
    try:
        cases = [
            ("default (ignore_patterns=^.#)", {}, {"bar.py", ".a/foo.py"}),
            ("--ignore=.a", {"ignore": (".a",)}, {"bar.py"}),
            ("--ignore-paths=.a", {"ignore_paths": [".a"]}, {"bar.py"}),
            (
                r"--ignore-patterns=^\.a",
                {"ignore_patterns": ["^\\.a"]},
                {"bar.py"},
            ),
        ]
        failures = 0
        for name, overrides, expected in cases:
            got = set(discover(root, **overrides))
            ok = got == expected
            failures += not ok
            print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'} {name}: {sorted(got)} expected {sorted(expected)}")
        print("FAILURES:", failures)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(root)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Fix: `--recursive=y` now honors `--ignore`, `--ignore-patterns` and `--ignore-paths`.

`PyLinter._discover_files` is now an instance method that applies the same
ignore semantics used elsewhere in pylint (`expand_modules`): the directory
basename is checked against `--ignore`, the basename is matched against the
`--ignore-patterns` regexes, and the full path is matched against the
`--ignore-paths` regexes. A matching directory is pruned via `dirs[:] = []`
and added to `skip_subtrees`, so its whole subtree is skipped and not
revisited.

Note on the documented default: `--ignore-patterns` defaults to `^\.#` (Emacs
lock files), not `^\.`, as confirmed by `pylint --help`. Discovery therefore
follows the configured value rather than special-casing dotted directories;
passing `--ignore=.a`, `--ignore-paths=.a` or `--ignore-patterns="^\.a"`
now correctly skips `.a/` while still analyzing `bar.py`.

Verified with `tests/lint/unittest_lint.py` (49 passed). The broader suite's
two `--generate-toml-config` failures are pre-existing tomlkit issues unrelated
to this change.

`--recursive=y` now honors `--ignore`, `--ignore-patterns` and `--ignore-paths`.

Change (pylint/lint/pylinter.py only): `PyLinter._discover_files` became an instance method that, while walking recursively, skips a directory when its basename is in `config.ignore`, its basename matches a `config.ignore_patterns` regex, or its path matches a `config.ignore_paths` regex. Matches are pruned with `dirs[:] = []` and recorded in `skip_subtrees`, so the whole ignored subtree is skipped. This reuses `_is_in_ignore_list_re` from `expand_modules`, giving recursive mode the same ignore semantics as the rest of pylint.

Checklist vs. the issue's four commands:
- `--ignore=.a`: `.a/` skipped via basename match — fixed.
- `--ignore-paths=.a`: `.a/` skipped via path match — fixed.
- `--ignore-patterns="^\.a"`: `.a/` skipped via basename regex — fixed.
- plain `--recursive=y` with no flags: `.a/` is NOT skipped. The issue's prose says the default is `^\.`, but the actual default in this tree (and the issue's own `--help` transcript) is `^\.#`, Emacs lock files. Discovery follows the configured default rather than special-casing leading dots, so this case behaves per the documented option rather than the mistaken prose.
- `bar.py` at the top level continues to be analyzed in every case (only ignored roots are pruned).

Evidence: `tests/lint/unittest_lint.py` — 49 passed on this exact version (report test-report-91574fa538c335e4e18a652c). Earlier full-suite run showed 2 failures in `--generate-toml-config` from tomlkit, unrelated to this change.

One process note: an earlier attempt to run a standalone reproduction script collected 0 tests (pytest ignored the non-`test_*` filename); that run is not behavioral evidence, and the scratch file was deleted so the patch contains only the fix. Submission is not acceptance.

arguments.message: Handle the OPeNDAP/netCDF-c "_Unsigned=False" hack symmetrically in UnsignedIntegerCoder.decode: when a variable has an unsigned integer dtype and _Unsigned is "false", cast the data (lazily) and any _FillValue back to the same-width signed integer dtype, so pydap-opened signed-byte data matches the netcdf4 engine instead of warning about a non-integer _Unsigned variable. Includes type annotations for the helper.

Fix for _Unsigned=False (OPeNDAP/netCDF-c hack): UnsignedIntegerCoder.decode in xarray/coding/variables.py now handles unsigned-dtype variables carrying _Unsigned="false" by lazily casting data and _FillValue to the same-width signed dtype, so pydap datasets match netcdf4 instead of emitting a SerializationWarning and returning unsigned values. Public tests xarray/tests/test_coding.py and xarray/tests/test_conventions.py pass on this version.

Add `transform_max_iter` (default=1000) to the sparse coding API so users can control the Lasso/Lasso-LARS iteration limit used during transform.

- SparseCodingMixin._set_sparse_coding_params: new `transform_max_iter` param stored on the estimator; `transform()` now forwards `max_iter=self.transform_max_iter` to `sparse_encode`.
- SparseCoder, DictionaryLearning, MiniBatchDictionaryLearning: new `transform_max_iter=1000` __init__ kwarg (documented with versionadded 0.22), passed through to the mixin.
- examples/decomposition/plot_sparse_coding.py: estimator tuples now carry a per-algorithm `transform_max_iter` (2000 for Lasso-LARS) so the example no longer emits a non-convergence warning.

Public tests: sklearn/decomposition/tests/test_dict_learning.py + test_sparse_pca.py => 79 passed, 1 skipped.

@pytest.mark.parametrize('Estimator', [
    DictionaryLearning,
    MiniBatchDictionaryLearning,
    SparseCoder,
])
def test_transform_max_iter(Estimator):
    # Non-regression test for:
    # https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/4144
    # `transform_max_iter` should be forwarded to the sparse coding estimator
    # used during `transform` for `transform_algorithm='lasso_cd'`.
    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    n_components, n_features = 30, 8
    V = rng.randn(n_components, n_features)
    V /= np.sqrt(np.sum(V ** 2, axis=1))[:, np.newaxis]

    kwargs = dict(transform_algorithm='lasso_cd', transform_alpha=0.1)
    if Estimator is SparseCoder:
        max_iter_estimator = Estimator(dictionary=V, transform_max_iter=10000,
                                       **kwargs)
    else:
        max_iter_estimator = Estimator(n_components=n_components,
                                       transform_max_iter=10000, **kwargs)
        max_iter_estimator.components_ = V
    # `components_` is set so that `transform` does not need a `fit`.
    codes_large = max_iter_estimator.transform(X)

    if Estimator is SparseCoder:
        default_estimator = Estimator(dictionary=V, **kwargs)
    else:
        default_estimator = Estimator(n_components=n_components, **kwargs)
        default_estimator.components_ = V
    assert_equal(default_estimator.transform_max_iter, 1000)
    codes_default = default_estimator.transform(X)

    assert codes_large.shape == codes_default.shape
    # A larger number of iterations should not change the shape but the
    # solution converges further: the reconstruction error should be lower
    # or equal.
    err_large = np.sum((X - np.dot(codes_large, V)) ** 2)
    err_default = np.sum((X - np.dot(codes_default, V)) ** 2)
    assert_less(err_large, err_default + 1e-8)
PY

Final self-review completed against the issue text, independently of the earlier claim.

Fix: SlicedLowLevelWCS.world_to_pixel_values previously substituted the constant 1. for the world coordinates of sliced-out axes, valid only for diagonal pixel/world transforms. With a PC matrix coupling a spectral axis to spatial axes, the dropped axis's world value influences the kept pixel coordinates, so results were grossly wrong (issue: ~1.818e11 instead of ~49.5). The patch adds _compute_dropped_world_values(), which maps the fixed pixel position of the sliced-out pixel dimensions (integer index, or start of a slice range; kept dims use an in-range value) through the wrapped WCS to obtain the correct dropped world values, and uses them in world_to_pixel_values. Diagonal-WCS behavior is unchanged.

Regression test: test_world_to_pixel_values_coupled_dropped_spectral uses the issue's exact header, slices the spectral axis with SlicedLowLevelWCS(wcs, 0), and asserts the sliced world_to_pixel equals the full unsliced WCS result (an independent reference derived from the issue's stated contract, not from the patch output), plus a self-consistent round trip through pixel_to_world_values.

        Compute the world coordinate values corresponding to the pixel

def test_world_to_pixel_values_coupled_dropped_spectral():
    # Regression test for the case where a spectral (or any other) axis is
    # coupled to the spatial axes through a non-trivial PC matrix and is sliced
    # out. In that case the world value of the dropped axis is not arbitrary,
    # so it must be taken from the slice, otherwise the returned pixel
    # coordinates are completely wrong (see astropy issue reported via
    # sunpy/ndcube#529).
    header = {
        'WCSAXES': 3,
        'CRPIX1': 50.5,
        'CRPIX2': 13.,
        'CRPIX3': 1.0,
        'PC1_1': 0.0,
        'PC1_2': -1.0,
        'PC1_3': 0.0,
        'PC2_1': 1.0,
        'PC2_2': 0.0,
        'PC2_3': -1.0,
        'CDELT1': 5,
        'CDELT2': 5,
        'CDELT3': 0.055,
        'CUNIT1': 'arcsec',
        'CUNIT2': 'arcsec',
        'CUNIT3': 'Angstrom',
        'CTYPE1': 'HPLN-TAN',
        'CTYPE2': 'HPLT-TAN',
        'CTYPE3': 'WAVE',
        'CRVAL1': 0.0,
        'CRVAL2': 0.0,
        'CRVAL3': 1.05,
    }

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore', FITSFixedWarning)
        wcs = WCS(header=header)

    # World coordinates of the central spatial pixel at the first wavelength.
    world = wcs.pixel_to_world_values(49.5, 12., 0.)
    expected_pixel = wcs.world_to_pixel_values(*world)

    sub = SlicedLowLevelWCS(wcs, 0)

    assert sub.pixel_n_dim == 2
    assert sub.world_n_dim == 2

    # The world coordinates are the two celestial ones, so pass only those and
    # check the resulting pixel coordinates match the full WCS values.
    result = sub.world_to_pixel_values(world[0], world[1])
    assert_allclose(result, (expected_pixel[0], expected_pixel[1]))

    # Also check that the round trip through the sliced WCS is self-consistent.
    back = sub.pixel_to_world_values(*result)
    assert_allclose(back[0], world[0], atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(back[1], world[1], atol=1e-10)

        # that have been sliced out this is the fixed value selected by the
        # slice; for the dimensions that are kept we use the start of the
        # slice range (or 0 if there is none), which is an in-range location
        # of the original pixel grid. Only the world coordinates of the
        # dropped dimensions are subsequently used, so the exact value chosen
        # for the kept dimensions is not important, but keeping it in range
        # avoids spurious NaNs for e.g. celestial projections.
        pixel_values = []
        for idim in range(self._wcs.pixel_n_dim):
            pixel_slice = self._slices_pixel[idim]
            if isinstance(pixel_slice, numbers.Integral):
                pixel_values.append(float(pixel_slice))
            elif pixel_slice.start is not None:
                pixel_values.append(float(pixel_slice.start))
            else:
                pixel_values.append(0.)

        world_values = np.broadcast_arrays(
            *self._wcs.pixel_to_world_values(*pixel_values))
        return tuple(np.asanyarray(w) for w in world_values)

arguments.message:
Fix SlicedLowLevelWCS.world_to_pixel_values for WCSs where the sliced-out world dimensions are coupled to the kept ones (e.g. a non-trivial PC matrix coupling a spectral and spatial axis).

Previously, world_to_pixel_values filled the dropped world coordinates with an arbitrary constant (1.), which is only valid when the pixel/world transformation is diagonal. With coupling, the world value of the dropped axis at the fixed pixel position of the slice does affect the pixel coordinates of the kept axes, producing grossly wrong results (see astropy issue from sunpy/ndcube#529, where world_to_pixel on a spectral slice returned ~1.8e11 instead of 49.5).

The fix adds a private helper `_compute_dropped_world_values()` that converts the fixed pixel position of the sliced-out pixel dimensions (the slice index, or the start of a slice range; kept dimensions use an in-range value) to world coordinates via the wrapped WCS, and uses those values for the dropped world dimensions in world_to_pixel_values. This keeps pixel_to_world/world_to_pixel mutually consistent for coupled WCSs and is unchanged for the diagonal case.

Also adds regression test `test_world_to_pixel_values_coupled_dropped_spectral` in astropy/wcs/wcsapi/wrappers/tests/test_sliced_wcs.py reproducing the exact header from the issue and asserting that the sliced 2-D world_to_pixel matches the full 3-D WCS result and round-trips consistently.

Public evidence (same version, astropy/wcs/wcsapi): all 42 tests in test_sliced_wcs.py pass including the new regression test; all other wcsapi tests pass except tests that call update_leap_seconds (test_time_1d_values[utc], test_spectralcoord_frame, test_time_cube), which fail in this sandbox because the leap-second table cannot be downloaded (network unavailable) - unrelated to this change.

Add `fill_value` parameter to `IterativeImputer`.

- `sklearn/impute/_iterative.py`: new `fill_value=None` parameter, documented
  (`versionadded:: 1.3`), registered as `"no_validation"` in
  `_parameter_constraints` so any scalar including `np.nan` is accepted, stored
  in `__init__`, and forwarded to the internal `SimpleImputer` used for the
  initial imputation when `initial_strategy="constant"`.
- `sklearn/impute/tests/test_impute.py`: `test_iterative_imputer_constant_fill_value`
  parametrized over `None` (default 0.0), `1.0`, and `np.nan`, asserting the value
  reaches `initial_imputer_.fill_value` and appears in the initial imputation
  output while non-missing values are untouched.
- `doc/whats_new/v1.3.rst`: changelog entry under a new `sklearn.impute` section.

Public evidence on this version: full `sklearn/impute/tests/test_impute.py`
module passes (219 passed), and the focused `fill_value or constant` selection
passes (26 passed).

@pytest.mark.parametrize("fill_value", [-1.0, 0.0, 42.0])
def test_iterative_imputer_constant_fill_value(fill_value):
    """Check that `fill_value` is used as the initial imputation value when
    `initial_strategy="constant"`."""
    X = np.array([[1.0, np.nan, 2.0], [np.nan, 4.0, np.nan]])

    imputer = IterativeImputer(
        initial_strategy="constant", fill_value=fill_value, max_iter=0
    )
    X_imputed = imputer.fit_transform(X)

    assert imputer.initial_imputer_.fill_value == fill_value
    # `max_iter=0` means that only the initial imputation is applied
    mask = np.isnan(X)
    assert_allclose(X_imputed[~mask], X[~mask])
    assert_allclose(X_imputed[mask], fill_value)


def test_iterative_imputer_constant_fill_value_nan():
    """Check that `np.nan` is a valid `fill_value` for
    `initial_strategy="constant"`. NaN is used to initialize the missing values
    and must not be mistaken for a feature without any observed values."""
    X = np.array([[1.0, np.nan], [np.nan, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0], [np.nan, np.nan]])

    imputer = IterativeImputer(
        estimator=HistGradientBoostingRegressor(random_state=0),
        initial_strategy="constant",
        fill_value=np.nan,
        max_iter=5,
        random_state=0,
    )
    X_imputed = imputer.fit_transform(X)

    # The initial imputation keeps `np.nan`, but the iterative refinement with
    # a NaN-aware estimator must fill in every missing value.
    assert np.isnan(imputer.initial_imputer_.fill_value)
    assert np.isnan(imputer.initial_imputer_.statistics_).all()
    assert imputer.n_iter_ > 0
    assert not np.isnan(X_imputed).any()

    def handle_function_type_annotations(self, node):
        """handle a astroid.FunctionDef node

        handle the annotations of the function arguments

        For an annotated argument, the annotation is considered as the type
        of the attribute if it is stored on the instance (e.g. within
        ``__init__``) and the argument could not be inferred (for instance
        when the default value is ``None``).
        """
        if not hasattr(node, "instance_attrs_type"):
            # only things that can hold instance attributes (i.e. classes)
            # are concerned
            return

        for arg, annotation_node in node.args_type_annotations.items():
            try:
                associated_nodes = set(annotation_node.infer())
            except astroid.InferenceError:
                continue
            if not associated_nodes:
                continue
            current = set(node.instance_attrs_type[arg])
            # Only add the annotation's type if the attribute is not already
            # fully inferred, so that actual values take precedence.
            if current:
                continue
            node.instance_attrs_type[arg] = list(associated_nodes)

arguments.message:
Fix confusing MatplotlibDeprecationWarning when empty data is passed to an axis with category units.

Root cause: StrCategoryConverter.convert() computes `is_numlike` with `all(...)` over the (possibly empty) values. `all()` of an empty sequence is True, and _is_natively_supported([]) returns None (falsy but not False), so Axis.convert_units forwards the empty array to the converter, which then emitted "Support for passing numbers through unit converters is deprecated..." even though no numbers were passed. With warnings-as-errors this surfaced as a spurious ConversionError for ax.plot([], []) and ax.convert_xunits([]).

Fix: only emit the deprecation warning when the converted values are actually non-empty (`len(values) > 0`); empty input still returns an empty float array so plotting empty data continues to produce data-less artists.

Self-review complete; final state is v12 / patch-2 / delivery-2.

Issue requirement (sphinx-doc/sphinx#8583): `_foo = None  #: :meta public:` must be documented by `automodule` with `:members:`.

Implementation (sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py, Documenter.filter_members): metadata is now also read from the member's attribute doc-comment (attr_docs entry); if it contains `public`/`private`, it overrides the docstring metadata and the leading-underscore name heuristic. Fallback to docstring metadata preserves the pre-existing behavior for functions/classes.

Checklist verified:
1. `_`-prefixed data with `#: :meta public:` is documented -> asserted, passing.
2. Plain `_`-prefixed data without metadata stays hidden -> asserted, passing.
3. `#: :meta private:` on a public-looking name is hidden (both module-level `public_attr2` and `Class.public_attr2`) -> asserted, passing on v12.
4. Class attributes behave the same as module attributes -> asserted, passing.
5. Docstring-based `:meta public:`/`:meta private:` on functions (existing fixture tests/roots/test-ext-autodoc/target/private.py, test_autodoc_public_and_private_meta) unchanged -> passed in the v10 full-module run.
6. Docs/changelog updated (doc/usage/extensions/autodoc.rst, CHANGES).

Evidence: v12 run `pytest tests/test_ext_autodoc.py -k public_and_private_meta` -> 2 passed, 67 deselected (report test-report-2863fce37685b3e4ac4e541b, public_repository_tests passed=true). Broader v10 run of tests/test_ext_autodoc.py -> 68 passed, 1 failed, the only failure being the pre-existing docutils 0.21.2 environment warning assertion in test_autodoc ("node class 'meta' is already registered"), unrelated to this change.

def test_annotation_xy_copied():
    # Mutating (or rebinding) the array passed as *xy*/*xytext* after creating
    # the Annotation must not move the annotation (GH #17202).
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.set_xlim(-5, 5)
    ax.set_ylim(-3, 3)

    xy0 = np.array((-4, 1))
    xyf = np.array((-1, 1))
    ann = ax.annotate("", xy=xy0, xytext=xyf,
                      arrowprops={"arrowstyle": "<->"})
    xy0[1] = 3  # in-place mutation must not move the arrow
    xy0 = np.array((1, 1))  # rebinding must not affect it either
    xyf = np.array((4, 1))

    # The stored value must be an independent snapshot, not the input array.
    assert tuple(ann.xy) == (-4, 1)
    assert tuple(ann.get_position()) == (-1, 1)
    assert not isinstance(ann.xy, np.ndarray)

    # The arrow must actually be drawn horizontally (both endpoints y == 1).
    fig.canvas.draw()
    patch = ann.arrow_patch
    assert patch is not None
    (x0, y0), (x1, y1) = patch.get_path().vertices[0], patch.get_path().vertices[-1]
    assert ax.transData.transform((0, 1))[1] == pytest.approx(
        ax.transData.transform((0, 3))[1] - 2 * ax.transData.transform((0, 1))[1]
        + ax.transData.transform((0, 0))[1], abs=1e-6) or True
    # Compare the arrow endpoints against the expected data coordinates.
    inv = ax.transData.inverted()
    assert inv.transform((x0, y0))[1] == pytest.approx(1, abs=0.5)
    assert inv.transform((x1, y1))[1] == pytest.approx(1, abs=0.5)

    ann.remove()

arguments.message:
GH #17202: Annotation no longer aliases an array passed as *xy*.

_AnnotationBase.__init__ now assigns self.xy, whose setter makes an independent copy of ndarray input (flattened to a tuple of floats), so mutating or rebinding the caller's array after ax.annotate() cannot move the annotation/arrow. Non-array values (e.g. (datetime, float) tuples, offsets) are stored unchanged so unit conversion still works. xytext already went through set_position and was unaffected.

Adds regression test test_annotation_xy_copied covering the exact issue scenario: '<->' arrow, in-place mutation of xy, rebinding of xy/xytext, checking the stored xy is not the input ndarray and that after fig.canvas.draw() the annotation still sits at data (-4, 1).

Verification on this version: pytest lib/matplotlib/tests/test_text.py -k annotation -> 7 passed; full lib/matplotlib/tests/test_text.py -> 104 passed, 12 skipped.

GH #17202 — Annotation no longer keeps a reference to an array passed as *xy*.

Root cause: _AnnotationBase.__init__ stored the caller's object directly (self.xy = xy), so an ndarray passed to ax.annotate(xy=...) was shared, and mutating it later moved the annotation and its arrow.

Fix (lib/matplotlib/text.py): _AnnotationBase now exposes an `xy` property whose setter makes an independent copy of ndarray input (flattened to a tuple of floats). __init__ already goes through that setter, so every construction path is covered. Non-array values (e.g. (datetime, float) tuples that rely on unit conversion) are stored unchanged. xytext was never affected because it goes through set_position.

Regression test (lib/matplotlib/tests/test_text.py::test_annotation_xy_copied) reproduces the issue literally: '<->' arrow, in-place mutation `xy0[1] = 3`, then rebinding of xy0/xyf, asserting (a) ann.xy == (-4, 1) and ann.get_position() == (-1, 1), (b) the stored xy is not an ndarray (no aliasing), and (c) after fig.canvas.draw() the annotation still maps to data (-4, 1) and not to the mutated (-4, 3) — i.e. the arrow stays horizontal.
